data.title: Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity
data.summary: An Oregon man is now in federal custody and charged in a criminal complaint with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity after he allegedly met a Utah minor online in May 2025, drove to Utah to pick up the victim, and then transported the victim to his residence across state lines.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/utah-mino.label: Utah Minor Recovered by Law Enforcement After Oregon Man Allegedly Transported the Victim to Engage in Criminal Sexual Activity

data.title: Los Angeles Woman Charged for $18M COVID-19 Relief Fraud Scheme
data.summary: A federal grand jury in the Central District of California returned an indictment yesterday charging Marisela Nuno, 53, of Los Angeles, California, with an $18 million scheme to defraud the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) and the Economic Injury Disaster Loan (EIDL) program, federal stimulus programs authorized as part of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/los-angel.label: Los Angeles Woman Charged for $18M COVID-19 Relief Fraud Scheme

data.title: Oklahoma Man Charged in Connection with Sending Threatening Letters Containing Non-Toxic White Powder to Election and Government Officials Across the Country
data.summary: Robin Patrick Martin, 67, of Oklahoma City, has been charged with conveying false or misleading information and hoaxes and mailing threatening communications in connection with threatening letters mailed to state election officials, members of Congress, the FBI and others.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/oklahoma-.label: Oklahoma Man Charged in Connection with Sending Threatening Letters Containing Non-Toxic White Powder to Election and Government Officials Across the Country

data.title: Former U.S. Government Contractor Pleads Guilty to Spying for Ethiopia
data.summary: Abraham Teklu Lemma, 53, of Maryland, a former information technology contractor at the National Reconnaissance Office, the U.S. Department of State, and the U.S. Department of Justice pleaded guilty today to conspiring to commit espionage on behalf of the government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/former-us.label: Former U.S. Government Contractor Pleads Guilty to Spying for Ethiopia

data.title: Defense and Aerospace Contractors ILC Dover and ILC Astrospace Agree to Pay $13M to Resolve Cybersecurity Fraud Allegations
data.summary: Defense and aerospace companies ILC Dover LP and ILC Astrospace LLC, of Frederica, Delaware, have agreed to pay $13 million to resolve allegations that they violated the False Claims Act by failing to comply with cybersecurity requirements in their contracts with the Department of the Army, the Missile Defense Agency, and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA).

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/defense-a.label: Defense and Aerospace Contractors ILC Dover and ILC Astrospace Agree to Pay $13M to Resolve Cybersecurity Fraud Allegations

data.title: Ohio Pet Breeder Agrees to Surrender Over 1,100 Chinchillas
data.summary: The U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Ohio endorsed a consent decree entered between the United States and the owner of R & R Chinchilla Inc. to surrender over 300 remaining chinchillas at a breeding facility in Jenera, Ohio. The court order follows R & R Chinchilla’s voluntary surrender of roughly 800 additional chinchillas to animal welfare organizations pursuant to a modified temporary restraining order.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/ohio-pet-.label: Ohio Pet Breeder Agrees to Surrender Over 1,100 Chinchillas

data.title: DOJ To Monitor Elections in All 50 States for First Time
data.summary: One of the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) most important missions is ensuring election integrity, supporting free and fair elections, and protecting the right to vote for U.S. citizens across the United States. The DOJ has sent election monitors in support of this mission since the enactment of the Voting Rights Act in 1965 across all Administrations.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/doj-monit.label: DOJ To Monitor Elections in All 50 States for First Time

data.title: American Man Extradited from Germany to Face Charges of Defrauding U.S. Consumers in Fake Psychic Mailing-Fraud Scheme
data.summary: Mael Chemla, 61, a U.S., French, and Israeli national, previously residing in Aventura, Florida, was extradited to the United States from Germany and made his initial appearance in Miami federal court yesterday to face charges for his role in operating a mailing fraud scheme.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/american-.label: American Man Extradited from Germany to Face Charges of Defrauding U.S. Consumers in Fake Psychic Mailing-Fraud Scheme

data.title: Lockheed Martin Agrees to Pay $29.5M to Resolve Alleged Employment Discrimination Violations
data.summary: Today, the U.S. Department of Justice and the U.S. Equal Employment Commission (EEOC) announced a two-part settlement against Lockheed Martin Corporation, headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland. Lockheed has agreed to pay a total of approximately $29.5 million to resolve allegations relating to employment discrimination and related false certifications of compliance with federal civil rights laws while serving as a federal contractor. This includes $22 million to be paid to the United States pursuant to an agreement with the Justice Department to resolve allegations that Lockheed violated the False Claims Act arising from failures to comply with anti-discrimination requirements in its federal contracts and by discriminating against employees and applicants on the basis of their race or sex. It also includes approximately $7.5 million to be paid to over 1,000 affected Lockheed employees pursuant to a negotiated settlement agreement with the EEOC resolving a 2025 Commissioner’s Charge filed by EEOC Chair Andrea Lucas, which alleged Lockheed violated Title VII of the Civil Rights Act by engaging in race discrimination against white employees, including in performance assessments and in bonus and other compensation decisions. This is the largest class of workers to publicly recover under an EEOC settlement on account of alleged Title VII violations arising from or relating to a DEI program or practices.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/lockheed-.label: Lockheed Martin Agrees to Pay $29.5M to Resolve Alleged Employment Discrimination Violations

data.title: Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 63 Individuals for Election-Related Crimes
data.summary: Today, the Justice Department announced charges involving 63 individuals, including four illegal aliens, in connection with illegal voting, fraudulent voter registration, and related election crimes across the country. The cases include voting by aliens in federal elections, false claims of U.S. citizenship to register to vote or to vote, and the fraudulent submission of a voter registration application in another state.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department Announces Charges Involving 63 Individuals for Election-Related Crimes

data.title: Florida Pharmacist Sentenced to Over 7 Years in Prison for Massive Illegal Oxycodone Distribution Conspiracy
data.summary: A Florida pharmacist and pharmacy owner was sentenced yesterday to 90 months in prison for her role in illegally dispensing over 300,000 oxycodone 30mg pills to pharmacy patrons who had no medical need for the drug.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/florida-p.label: Florida Pharmacist Sentenced to Over 7 Years in Prison for Massive Illegal Oxycodone Distribution Conspiracy

data.title: Botox Fraud Doctor Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for $45M Medicare Scheme
data.summary: California doctor Violetta Mailyan was sentenced yesterday to 15 years in prison for using her medical practice to fraudulently bill Medicare more than $45 million for Botox injection services that were medically unnecessary and never provided.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/botox-fra.label: Botox Fraud Doctor Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for $45M Medicare Scheme

data.title: Indian National Pleads Guilty to $227M Medicare Fraud
data.summary: An Indian national pleaded guilty today to a $227 million Medicare fraud scheme in which hundreds of thousands of Medicare beneficiaries’ personally identifiable information was purchased from a company based in Pakistan and used to bill Medicare for COVID-19 test kits that were never provided.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/indian-na.label: Indian National Pleads Guilty to $227M Medicare Fraud

data.title: Israeli National Extradited to Face Charges for Stealing Nearly $3M in Virtual Currency Heist
data.summary: Alexander Gurevich, 49, an Israeli national, had his initial appearance today in the Northern District of California on a 2023 indictment that charged him for exploiting the Nomad Bridge’s self-executing computer program, also known as a smart contract, to steal $2.89 million in virtual currency.

data.title: California Man Pleads Guilty to Attempting to Provide Material Support to the Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham
data.summary: Ammaad Akhtar, 34, of California, pleaded guilty today to attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/californi.label: California Man Pleads Guilty to Attempting to Provide Material Support to the Islamic State of Iraq and al-Sham

data.summary: The Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division (Fraud Division), and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Minnesota announced a series of enforcement actions targeting fraud involving taxpayer-funded Medicaid and SNAP programs.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/dojs-frau.label: DOJ’s Fraud Division and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District Minnesota Uncover Nearly $30M in Benefits Fraud in Enforcement Surge

data.title: Justice Department Announces Nearly $300 Million in Awards to Four Model Cities to Combat Violent Crime and Restore Law and Order
data.summary: Today, the Justice Department announced the selection of four jurisdictions to receive nearly $300 million in federal funding through its Model Cities Initiative (MCI), a flagship effort to reduce violent crime, restore law and order, and strengthen public safety in American communities.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department Announces Nearly $300 Million in Awards to Four Model Cities to Combat Violent Crime and Restore Law and Order

data.title: Justice Department Announces Issuance of Federal Registrations for Medical Marijuana Dispensaries
data.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice today announced that the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is moving forward with the initial issuance of hundreds of federal registrations to qualifying state-licensed medical marijuana dispensaries under the Attorney General’s order implementing Schedule III controls for certain medical marijuana activities.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department Announces Issuance of Federal Registrations for Medical Marijuana Dispensaries

data.title: Justice Department Defends the Navy’s Actions to Address a Fuel Release at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam in Hawaii
data.summary: The U.S. District Court for the District of Hawaii earlier this week ruled that the U.S. Navy is not in violation of the Clean Water Act after it reviewed the Navy’s response to fuel releases in 2020 and 2021 at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam on Oahu, Hawaii, and other substantial improvements the Navy has made in the fueling infrastructure and operations. The ruling follows a bench trial that was held earlier this year regarding claims that the Navy is in violation of the Clean Water Act at the Joint Base.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/justice-d.label: Justice Department Defends the Navy’s Actions to Address a Fuel Release at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam in Hawaii

data.title: Former Correctional Officer Sentenced on Federal Civil Rights Charges in Connection with Conspiracy to Violate Inmates’ Rights at West Virginia Jail
data.summary: A former correctional officer from the Southern Regional Jail in Beaver, West Virginia, was sentenced today to 24 months in prison for his role in a conspiracy in which he and other correctional officers used unreasonable and unjustified force against inmates, including pretrial detainees, as a form of punishment and retaliation. Michael Pack, 40, pleaded guilty on March 30 before U.S. Magistrate Judge Omar J. Aboulhosn to one count of violating 18 U.S.C. § 371.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/former-co.label: Former Correctional Officer Sentenced on Federal Civil Rights Charges in Connection with Conspiracy to Violate Inmates’ Rights at West Virginia Jail

data.title: Former U.S. Government Contractor Arrested for Allegedly Leaking National Defense Information and Stealing Night Vision Goggles
data.summary: James Thomas Ashbacher, 37, of Spring Lake, North Carolina, a former U.S. government contractor, was arrested by the FBI on Tuesday for allegedly leaking national defense information by posting the information on a popular social media site, unlawfully retaining other national defense information at his residence, and stealing night vision goggles from the U.S. Army’s Special Operations Command.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/former-us.label: Former U.S. Government Contractor Arrested for Allegedly Leaking National Defense Information and Stealing Night Vision Goggles

data.title: Former BizJet Sales Manager Pleads Guilty to Foreign Bribery
data.summary: Jald Jensen, 73, of Panama City, and previously of Van Nuys, California, a former sales manager of BizJet International Sales and Support Inc. (BizJet), pleaded guilty yesterday for his role in connection with a scheme to pay bribes to government officials in Latin America to secure business for BizJet.

https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/former-bi.label: Former BizJet Sales Manager Pleads Guilty to Foreign Bribery
